Estimate Heterogeneous Treatment Effects (CATE) via DR-Learner

Source: R/cate_and_sim.R
fit_cate.Rd

Feeds the doubly-robust Efficient Influence Function pseudo-outcomes from a fitted "tmle_fit" object into a second-stage tidymodels regression workflow or Super Learner (Kennedy, 2023) to estimate Conditional Average Treatment Effects \(\tau(V) = E[Y(1) - Y(0) \mid V]\).

Usage

fit_cate(fit, learners = "default", covariates = NULL, v_folds = 5L)

# S3 method for class 'tmle_cate'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tmle_cate'
augment(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

A fitted "tmle_fit" object with binary treatment.

learners

"default", a parsnip model_spec (regression mode), a workflow, a workflow_set, or a list of specs/workflows.

covariates

Optional character vector or tidyselect expression of effect modifiers \(V \subseteq W\). Defaults to all baseline covariates from fit.

v_folds

Number of cross-fitting folds for out-of-fold CATE evaluation and Best Linear Projection heterogeneity testing (default 5L).

x

A fitted "tmle_cate" object passed to tidy() or augment().

...

Additional arguments (currently unused).

Value

An S3 object of class "tmle_cate" supporting predict(), tidy(), augment(), autoplot(), and qini_auc().

Details

Because the individual treatment effect \(Y_i(1) - Y_i(0)\) is never directly observed, Kennedy's Doubly Robust (DR) Learner constructs the cross-fitted pseudo-outcome $$\varphi_i = H_i \left(Y_i - \bar{Q}^*(A_i, W_i)\right) + \left(\bar{Q}^*(1, W_i) - \bar{Q}^*(0, W_i)\right)$$ whose conditional expectation given covariates \(V\) equals the true CATE \(\tau(V)\) whenever either \(\bar{Q}\) or \(g\) is consistently estimated. Regressing \(\varphi_i\) on \(V_i\) lets any tidymodels regression workflow learn treatment effect heterogeneity while tidy() reports Chernozhukov et al.'s (2018) Best Linear Projection (BLP) test for significant effect modification.

References

Kennedy, E. H. (2023). Towards optimal doubly robust estimation of heterogeneous causal effects. Electronic Journal of Statistics, 17(2), 3008–3049.

Chernozhukov, V., Demirer, M., Duflo, E., & Fernandez-Val, I. (2018). Generic machine learning inference on heterogeneous treatment effects in randomized experiments. NBER Working Paper No. 24678.

Examples

df <- sim_causal_cohort(n = 200, outcome_type = "continuous", seed = 42)
fit <- tmle_spec(y, a, c(age, sex, lab_1, lab_2)) |>
  set_resamples(v_folds = 3L) |>
  fit(df)
cate <- fit_cate(fit, v_folds = 3L)
tidy(cate)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   term         estimate std.error statistic  p.value conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 ATE (BLP In…    2.16      0.238      9.08 1.14e-16    1.69      2.63 
#> 2 Heterogenei…    0.337     0.239      1.41 1.60e- 1   -0.134     0.808
qini_auc(cate)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   .metric  .estimator .estimate
#>   <chr>    <chr>          <dbl>
#> 1 qini_auc standard       0.109
#> 2 auuc     standard       1.19
